verdict: Thermo Fisher grew revenue 9% to $12.1B, powered by a 15% jump in lab products and pharma services, and kept $1.7B as profit despite $199M of restructuring costs.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $12.1B vs $11.1B a year ago; organic growth (excluding deals and currency) was 6%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: up 9% YoY; adjusted EPS $6.68 excluding amortization and restructuring

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: operating cash flow $2.55B minus $437M of plant & equipment spending

segments.name: Laboratory Products & Biopharma Services
segments.note: Lab supplies, equipment and channels, plus pharma services and clinical research — the biggest and fastest-growing business, over half of revenue.

segments.name: Life Sciences Solutions
segments.note: Reagents, instruments and consumables used in biology research and biotech production.

segments.name: Analytical Instruments
segments.note: Precision instruments — chromatography, mass spectrometry and electron microscopes.

segments.name: Specialty Diagnostics
segments.note: Clinical and specialty diagnostic tests — down mainly because the microbiology business was sold during the quarter; its revenue halved to $70M.

segments.name: Eliminations
segments.note: Sales between Thermo Fisher's own segments, removed so revenue is not double-counted. The filing reports eliminations of $546M; its segment lines, rounded to $M, total $1M less than consolidated revenue, and this reconciling line absorbs that $1M.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative — the sales force, marketing and running the company.

opex.name: Intangible amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of patents, brands and customer relationships from past acquisitions over their lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new instruments, tests and services.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: Severance, asset impairments and facility-consolidation charges from an ongoing cost-cutting program.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $417M, partly offset by $252M of interest income, plus $10M of other expense — a net $175M cost. A further $9M of equity losses and $6M of profit belonging to noncontrolling interests are deducted to reach the $1,721M attributable to Thermo Fisher shareholders (total net income was $1,727M).
oneTimers: Restructuring and other costs of $199M (severance, impairments and facility consolidations; about 2% of the workforce affected by the wider program) are excluded from adjusted results, as is $519M of acquisition-related intangible amortization — together they explain most of the gap between GAAP EPS of $4.64 and adjusted EPS of $6.68.
Thermo Fisher completed the sale of its microbiology business during the quarter, which is why Specialty Diagnostics revenue fell even as the rest of the company grew.
footerNote: Segment revenues are as reported in $M; the filing's segment lines and its reported $546M of intersegment eliminations total $12,136M vs consolidated revenue of $12,137M, a $1M rounding difference absorbed in the eliminations line above.

takeaways.title: Pharma services are the engine
takeaways.text: Laboratory Products & Biopharma Services grew 15% to $6,863M — clinical research revenue alone rose 21% to $2,445M — and now supplies 57% of all revenue.

takeaways.title: Diagnostics shrank on a sale, not demand
takeaways.text: Specialty Diagnostics fell 6% to $1,098M, mainly because the microbiology business was divested in the quarter (its revenue dropped from $162M to $70M).

takeaways.title: Two profit numbers, one business
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $6.68 vs GAAP $4.64 — the $2.04 gap is mostly $519M of non-cash acquisition amortization and $199M of restructuring charges that adjusted results strip out.
